name: btn
summary: Check whether a button is held down.
note: Indices: 0 left, 1 right, 2 up, 3 down, 4 B, 5 A, 6 Start, 7 Select, 8 L, 9 R. Invalid indices return false. In the editor preview, Z is A and X is B. System pause starts disabled. pause(true) reserves Start; pause(false) lets btn(6)/btnp(6) handle it normally in menus. Game input and button-repeat ticks freeze only during active pause.

name: btnp
summary: React to a button press, with held-button repeat.
note: Fires on held tick 1, then 15, 19, 23, and every four held ticks thereafter. Releasing resets the counter. Use btn() for continuous movement. Start is ordinary input unless the game opts into system pause with pause(true).

name: spr
signature: spr(id, x, y [, w, h, flip_x, flip_y])
summary: Draw a cell or rectangle from the shared sprite sheet.
note: Use spr for shared-sheet tiles and simple sheet-based objects, especially artwork also used by a map. Sprite cells are 8×8 pixels. Position is the top-left corner; width and height are in cells. Color 0 is transparent by default. Create the artwork in Sprite Lab → Shared Tiles first. If an object's tile layout and offsets should be reusable editor assets, draw an authored pose with pspr. If it should play an ordered sequence of poses, use anim.

name: sspr
signature: sspr(sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy [, dw, dh, flip_x, flip_y])
summary: Draw a rectangular part of the sprite sheet.
note: Source coordinates and sizes are in pixels. Scaling or arbitrary crops require the bitmap renderer; aligned, unscaled rectangles may use hardware sprites.

name: pspr
summary: Draw one authored pose: a reusable image assembled from tiles.
note: Use pspr for a static character frame, prop, effect, or UI element whose tile layout and offsets belong in Sprite Lab rather than repeated Lua spr calls. A pose may combine several tile parts; pspr draws that one pose and does not advance frames. Use anim for a timed pose sequence. Register hero_idle in Sprite Lab → Poses first, then use COPY LUA CALL. Prefer a case-sensitive literal pose name: the build resolves it to the current index with no runtime lookup or name storage. Other poses can be deleted or reordered without changing the call. Missing literal names fail the build with a source position and a close spelling suggestion when available. Names must be string literals, optionally parenthesized; dynamic string lookup and generated symbols are not supported. Existing zero-based numeric IDs still work, but deletion shifts later IDs. Out-of-range numeric literals emit nonfatal build warnings after normal 16:16 conversion; invalid dynamic numeric IDs draw nothing. The origin and offsets come from the recipe; flips mirror within its calculated tile bounds. Poses use objsheet.json when present, otherwise the shared sheet. Mode 0 still requires a proven working set and hardware resource budgets; choosing a pose alone does not guarantee eligibility.

name: anim
signature: anim(name, x, y [, flip_x [, flip_y [, elapsed_seconds]]])
summary: Draw a timed sequence of poses using an authored animation clip.
note: Use anim for walking, flying, pickups, attacks, or other ordered pose sequences: the editor owns the frame order, FPS, and loop setting instead of Lua frame-index arithmetic. Use pspr for one static pose. Register idle in Sprite Lab → Animations before building. Without elapsed_seconds, calls use the shared game clock and identical clips stay synchronized. Switching the clip name does not restart it: anim is stateless. For an action or independent entity, store started when the action begins and supply time() - started; do not reset started every draw. Negative elapsed time selects the first frame; nonlooping clips hold their final frame. Flips use a fixed rectangle across every pose in the clip. Unknown literal names fail the build; unknown dynamic names or empty clips draw nothing. No entity or playback state is allocated.

name: pvariant
summary: Select a named color variant for subsequent pose and animation draws.
example:
pvariant("alternate")
anim("idle", 100, 60)
pvariant() -- restore original colors
note: Create alternate in Sprite Lab → Poses → Color Variants. Variants are project-wide simultaneous palette-index replacements; index 0 remains transparent. They affect pspr and anim, not spr or maps, and remain active across frames until reset. Numeric IDs are 1-based; prefer names when editing the library. Unknown literal names fail builds; unknown dynamic names/IDs reset original colors. Mode 0 may share 4bpp pixels with separate hardware palettes; Mode 4 compiles recolored artwork. Exact resource and call-shape restrictions are in the renderer contract.

name: sget
summary: Read a palette index from the sprite sheet.
note: This reads authored sheet pixels, not the finished screen.

name: sset
summary: Change a pixel in the sprite sheet.
note: This changes the game’s runtime copy. It does not save artwork back to your project. Hardware rendering requires bounded mutation placement; see the renderer contract.

name: fget
summary: Read a sprite’s flags.
note: With a flag index, reads that bit; without it, returns the flag byte. Flags are useful for labeling solid or collectible tiles.

name: fset
summary: Change a sprite’s flags.
note: A flag affects the logical sprite and later map filtering. Runtime mutation can change AUTO renderer selection.

name: map
signature: map() / map(bg [, cx, cy, x, y, w, h, mask])
summary: Draw the tile maps you created in the editor.
note: map() draws all authored non-empty planes, back to front. With arguments, the first is always a literal BG0–BG3 layer. Do not mix automatic and explicit forms. Source-cell offsets contribute to world positions; read the map contract before scrolling a subsection.

name: mget
summary: Read the sprite ID in a map cell.
note: Map coordinates are in 8×8 cells. The two-argument form uses BG0. Invalid coordinates or absent planes return 0.

name: mset
signature: mset(x, y, id) / mset(bg, x, y, id)
summary: Replace a map cell while the game runs.
note: The three-argument form edits BG0. Runtime edits are not saved into project files. Invalid coordinates are ignored.

name: camera
summary: Move the view without moving your game objects.
note: The camera position is subtracted from drawing coordinates. camera() resets the view. Keep world coordinates separate from screen coordinates.

name: cls
summary: Clear the screen for a new frame.
note: Colors are palette indices. In Aurora, 24 is dark blue and 15 is white. Put one unconditional cls() at the start of _draw() for hardware-renderer eligibility.

name: print
summary: Draw text or a number on the screen.
note: This explicit four-argument form is the easiest to start with. Separate labels and numeric values to keep them eligible for hardware rendering. Text uses a 6×8 cell font; Mode 0 has additional glyph and object limits.

name: pset
summary: Set one screen pixel.
note: Screen coordinates start at (0, 0) in the top-left. The screen is 240 pixels wide and 160 high.

name: pget
summary: Read a color from the composed screen.
note: The result reflects drawing that has already happened. Use sget() to inspect the sprite sheet instead.

name: line
summary: Draw a straight line between two points.
note: The current camera and clipping rectangle apply to the line.

name: rect
summary: Draw a rectangle outline.
note: The last two coordinates are the opposite corner, not width and height. The endpoints are inclusive.

name: rectfill
summary: Draw a filled rectangle.
note: Use opposite-corner coordinates. Drawing a filled rectangle is a bitmap-renderer operation.

name: circ
summary: Draw a circle outline.
note: The first two coordinates are the center. The radius is measured in pixels.

name: circfill
summary: Draw a filled circle.
note: Useful for quick prototypes and particles; this selects bitmap rendering.

name: color
summary: Set the default drawing color.
note: Explicit color arguments override the default. cls() does not change it.

name: cursor
summary: Set the text cursor position and optional color.
note: Explicitly positioned print() calls are usually clearer for a first game.

name: clip
summary: Limit drawing to a rectangle.
note: clip() restores full-screen drawing. Smaller clipping rectangles require Mode 4 in the current hardware-renderer subset.

name: pal
summary: Remap one palette color to another.
note: Bank 0 (default) remaps subsequent drawing; bank 1 remaps the displayed palette, including already drawn pixels. pal(bank) resets that bank. pal() resets both banks and restores default transparency. Only banks 0 and 1 are supported. Mode 0 imposes placement and remapping restrictions; see the renderer contract.

name: palt
summary: Control which sprite colors are transparent.
note: The default makes palette index 0 transparent in sprites and maps. Arbitrary transparent colors require Mode 4.

name: sfx
summary: Play a short sound-effect clip.
note: Create an SFX clip with this ID in Audio first, or use Coin Quest’s included clip 0. Default priority is 160. sfx(-1) stops gameplay-owned effects.

name: music
summary: Start a song from the Audio workspace.
note: Create a song with this ID first. music(-1) stops song-owned notes while leaving gameplay effects independent.

name: gba_note
summary: Play a hardware note using a saved sound.
note: Channels are 1–4. The sound must match the channel. Timed notes use 96 ticks per quarter note; zero duration sustains until stopped.

name: gba_stop
summary: Stop notes on a hardware channel.
note: Use channel numbers 1–4. This is a direct channel command; music and effects share these hardware channels.

name: flr
summary: Round down to an integer.
note: flr(-1.5) is -2, not -1. Use it when converting pixel coordinates into map cells.

name: ceil
summary: Round up to an integer.
note: ceil(-1.5) is -1. Numbers in mTile use 16:16 fixed point.

name: abs
summary: Get the distance of a number from zero.
note: abs(-8) is 8. Handy for simple collision checks.

name: sgn
summary: Return -1 for a negative number, or 1 otherwise.
note: sgn(0) returns 1.

name: min
summary: Choose the smaller of two numbers.
note: Use this to cap a value at an upper limit.

name: max
summary: Choose the larger of two numbers.
note: Use this to keep a value above a lower limit.

name: mid
summary: Choose the middle value of three numbers.
note: Putting a value between its lower and upper bounds clamps it to that range.

name: sin
summary: Get the vertical sine component of a turn.
note: Angles use turns, not degrees or radians. sin(0.25) is -1, matching a screen where Y increases downward.

name: cos
summary: Get the horizontal cosine component of a turn.
note: One complete turn is 1. cos(0) is 1.

name: atan2
summary: Find a direction angle in turns.
note: Uses the screen-coordinate convention shared with sin() and cos().

name: sqrt
summary: Find a square root.
note: Zero and negative inputs return 0. Fixed-point precision is finite; squared distances can avoid square roots when comparing distances.

name: rnd
summary: Choose a pseudorandom fixed-point number.
note: The numeric form ranges from zero up to, but excluding, a positive limit. rnd() uses a limit of 1; a zero or negative limit returns 0. Table-item selection is not implemented: choose an index with flr(rnd(#items)) + 1 for a nonempty list.

name: srand
summary: Set the random-number seed.
note: A fixed seed makes random sequences repeatable for testing.

name: add
summary: Append or insert a value into a list.
note: Lua list indices start at 1. Insertion shifts the existing elements.

name: del
summary: Remove the first matching value from a list.
note: Searches the contiguous list first and shifts it when removing an item; if no list match exists, also searches named/hash entries. Returns the removed value, or nil when absent. Use deli() to remove by list index.

name: deli
summary: Remove an element by its list index.
note: With no index, removes the final element.

name: count
summary: Count the list prefix or matching table values.
note: Without a value (or with nil), returns the contiguous numbered length, stopping at the first nil. With a non-nil value, counts matches across occupied array and hash slots, including named fields.

name: all
signature: for value in all(table) do ... end
summary: Visit each value in a list.
example:
total = 0
for value in all({10, 20, 30}) do
  total += value
end -- total is 60
note: all() is iterator syntax here. Do not assign the iterator itself to a variable.

name: pairs
signature: for key, value in pairs(table) do ... end
summary: Visit a table’s keys and values.
example:
total = 0
for key, value in pairs({score=5}) do
  total += value
end -- total is 5
note: Do not rely on a particular traversal order.

name: foreach
summary: Call a function for each list element.
example:
total = 0
function accumulate(value)
  total += value
end
foreach({10, 20}, accumulate) -- total is 30
note: Use a named, statically bound callback. Read the foreach guide for mutation rules.

name: sub
summary: Take a section of a string.
note: Indices start at 1 and the final index is inclusive. String operations are byte-oriented.

name: tostr
summary: Convert a value to text.
note: For Mode 0 text, print numeric values directly instead of passing a converted string.

name: tonum
summary: Convert numeric text to a number.
note: Invalid or nonnumeric input returns nil; test the result before arithmetic. Numeric input is returned unchanged.

name: chr
summary: Create a one-byte string from a character code.
note: 65 is uppercase A. This is a byte operation, not a Unicode conversion.

name: ord
summary: Read a byte’s numeric character code.
note: Indices start at 1. An index outside the string returns nil.

name: time
summary: Read elapsed game time in seconds.
note: t() is an alias. This is game time, not the computer’s wall clock.

name: t
summary: Read elapsed game time in seconds.
note: An alias for time().

name: stat
summary: Read runtime performance counters.
note: stat(1) is the previous tick’s share of the roughly 30 Hz frame budget: 1 means the entire budget. It is not host CPU percentage. See the performance guide for other counters.

name: printh
summary: Accept a compatibility call without producing output.
note: Currently a no-op in compiled games and the editor ROM preview. Arguments are evaluated, but no console log or file is written. Use print() in _draw() to display a value on screen.

name: band
summary: Bitwise AND.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bor
summary: Bitwise OR.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bxor
summary: Bitwise exclusive OR.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bnot
summary: Invert the bits of a number.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: shl
summary: Shift bits left.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: shr
summary: Shift bits right with sign extension.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: lshr
summary: Shift bits right without sign extension.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: rotl
summary: Rotate bits left.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: rotr
summary: Rotate bits right.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: save_set
summary: Stage a numeric field for the next cartridge save.
note: Fields are 0..63 and store exact signed 16:16 numbers. Returns true for a valid integer index and numeric value, false otherwise. This only changes RAM. Use save_write to commit. See the dedicated cartridge saving guide.

name: save_get
summary: Read a numeric field from the save staging buffer.
note: Fields start at zero. Invalid types, fractional indices, and indices outside 0..63 return 0. A successful save_read fills all 64 fields; an unsuccessful read leaves them unchanged. Renderer-independent.

name: save_read
summary: Restore one independent cartridge save slot into the staging buffer.
example: if save_read("my-game-v1", active_slot) == 1 then score = save_get(0) end
note: Slots are integer numbers 0..31; omitted means slot 0, preserving the original format. Dynamic slots evaluate once. The key must be a literal string of 1..32 bytes. Returns 1 on success, 0 for blank records, -2 for corrupt/unsupported records, -3 for a different key, -5 for an invalid slot, or -1 for missing runtime storage. Failed reads preserve the buffer. Test == 1 explicitly: zero and negative numbers are truthy in Lua. Two recovery copies belong to each slot. Renderer-independent; physical verification remains pending.

name: save_write
summary: Write and verify all 64 staged fields in one independent cartridge slot.
note: Slots are integer numbers 0..31; omitted means slot 0. The key must be a literal string of 1..32 bytes. Returns 1 for verified cartridge-visible bytes, -1 on verification failure, or -5 for an invalid slot. Alternates two recovery records within this slot and commits last; other slots are untouched. Failed writes preserve staged progress. An explicit write can replace damaged data or another key: offer deliberate confirmation. Success restarts save_pending for 150 engine polls, including during pause, without blocking Start resume. On original EZ-Flash Omega, wait five seconds before power-off/reset. This timer cannot acknowledge microSD completion. Renderer-independent.

name: save_pending
summary: Check the five-second power-off reminder after a successful save.
example: if save_pending() then print("PLEASE WAIT", 84, 76, 7) end
note: Returns a boolean. True for 150 engine polls (about five seconds at 30 Hz) after each successful save_write, including while paused. A failed write neither clears nor restarts a previous reminder. It never blocks pause/resume. This is a timed reminder for cartridge procedures, not a hardware busy bit or proof of SD flush completion. Renderer-independent; it does not allocate save storage by itself.

name: pause
summary: Enable or disable the fixed Start pause during gameplay.
example:
pause(true) -- Gameplay
pause(false) -- Title / file / inventory menus
note: Disabled by default. Accepts one boolean and returns no values; other types are ignored. The setting takes effect at the next engine input poll. While enabled, Start freezes the game behind the fixed centered PAUSED message, and a second Start resumes. While disabled, btn(6) and btnp(6) receive Start normally. A Start press held through enabling must be released and pressed again to pause. Disabling an active pause restores graphics in the normal presentation window before gameplay resumes. Only availability is configurable; appearance and controls stay fixed. Renderer-independent; system OBJ resources remain reserved even while disabled.
